signals.statement: Original and later-comparative FY2024 disclosed server ASP/units percentages differ.
signals.inference: Comparison vintage joins must gate historical ASP indices; a default latest-only series loses valuable contradictory data.
signals.alternative: A specific segment recast or rounding could resolve the apparent conflict; formal reconciliation remains required.

signals.statement: R770 and R7725 published CPU option ladders are additive across different selected default CPUs.
signals.inference: Build relative SKU-pair shadow option prices from Dell rather than compare base-dependent options raw; cannot infer Dell processor acquisition costs.
signals.alternative: Same Dell product pricing system could cause identical ladder despite disparate co-requisite configuration costs.

questions.question: Why did the original FY2024 Intel server ASP YoY +12%, volume -10% become +11%, -8% in the later FY2025 comparative?
questions.method: Audit original vs comparative metric scope and segment restatement explanations in both 10-Ks and accounting notes; preserve both until specific cause confirmed.
questions.decision_impacted: Avoid silently chaining non-equivalent disclosed ASP growth factors.

questions.question: Can we obtain two immutable independently timestamped original SKU price snapshots and fully BOM-normalized OEM cart totals?
questions.method: Implement archival hash capture and full-co-requisite quote capture; rerun matched-SKU panel on two true dates.
questions.decision_impacted: Move from one descriptive reference comparison toward defensible actual price index.

questions.question: Can public buyer-specific x86 server CPU net semiconductor prices or matching pure CPU revenue/physical units be identified?
questions.method: Audit government and OEM BOM-level awards and volume sources; refuse CPU net invoice estimates if missing.

conflicts.issue: FY2024 Intel server ASP growth is +12% in original FY2024 10-K versus +11% in FY2025 comparative; FY2024 server volume -10% vs -8%; reporting methodology and comparability unresolved.
conflicts.resolution_plan: Review 2024 vs 2025 Intel reported server metric definitions, restated DCAI scope, notes and investor IR; preserve original and comparative if incompatible.

methods.name: Two-model OEM CPU configurator price-ladder normalization
methods.procedure: For two configurations with same OEM/model/region/currency/price basis but differing selected baseline, compute SKU s relative to reference r: (option_a(s)-option_a(r))-(option_b(s)-option_b(r)); require <=1 EUR cent across overlapping available SKUs; missing/unavailable stays null. Failing co-requisite verification means only quote-internal price ladder agreement, not actual paid hardware totals.
inputs: OEM model, region, selected baseline, source, listed availability and EUR cent integers
methods.output: Matched-SKU relative option spreads and residuals; supplier procurement price NEVER inferred.

methods.name: Original vs comparative filing ASP conflict detection
methods.procedure: Group by publisher, metric, FY comparison, denominator, then retain each dated filing vintage. Emit conflict if percent different, do not create a single market series without resolution.

requirements.name: Immutable public SKU and configured-cart snapshot capture
requirements.user_outcome: Local ZCode agents can archive authorized source renders with UTC timestamp, raw SHA, parsed SKU, region, tax, quantity basis, co-requisites and reproducible normalized quotes.
acceptance_criteria: Two dated original snapshots for same SKU, not merely two content caches
Mark all mutable sources unarchived until hash capture
Do not automatically promote a price to CPU market actuals
Collect all forced BOM co-requisites and chosen socket count

promotions.decision_note: Hold due to FY2024 original-vs-2025 comparative +12/+11 conflict; no overwrite of preexisting +11 vintage.
Per-SKU live 1KU reference belongs in future pricing snapshot warehouse, not revenue/shipments macro series.
OEM selected-option premium not same as chip net ASP; preserve typed data/pricing/run-01 only.
Reusable run design already recorded in methodology/runbook; not a promoted measured market series.
